postmortem.diagnosis: VALIDATED LIVE-FLOW UNDER. Scoring regressed upward after halftime rather than remaining frozen at first-half levels, yet the market total still proved materially too high. The game produced 81 second-half points versus approximately 76 implied by the frozen SharpEdge projection; final total 151 finished 5 points above model but 10.5 below the wager line. Fourth-quarter scoring accelerated to 48 points with both teams shooting 56.2% FG, highlighting garbage-time/bench-efficiency risk in large-spread live unders, but the entry retained an 11-point cushion relative to the 92 second-half points required to lose.
postmortem.lesson: Do not require cold first-half shooting to persist. The strongest live-under setup is one where reasonable shooting regression can occur and the live number still carries a large structural cushion. Continue tracking late-game garbage-time scoring as an explicit volatility factor when the favorite leads by 15+ at halftime.

notes: Primary LIVE-FLOW strike. Frozen projection was established before market reveal. Official final: NYL 85, CHI 66. William Hill ticket settled WON at -120.

postmortem.end_q3_context: Phoenix led 88-49 (+39) after scoring 30 in the third quarter. Through three quarters Phoenix was 53.3% FG and 53.8% from three, while Toronto was 34.1% FG and 20.0% from three. Phoenix had also generated 28 fast-break points and Toronto had committed 14 turnovers.
postmortem.q4_regime: Extreme blowout produced a full bench/garbage-time rotation. Phoenix's starters did not play in the fourth quarter; Phoenix scored only 13 on 29.4% FG and 12.5% 3P, while Toronto scored 20 on 44.4% FG. The combined fourth-quarter total was 33.
postmortem.diagnosis: WINNING Q4 LIVE-FLOW UNDER with a modest model-to-market gap but favorable blowout-state compression. The frozen SharpEdge final total was 174; the executed 176.5 line created 2.5 points of model separation and the game finished 170, four points below model and 6.5 below the wager line. The critical mechanism was asymmetric garbage-time allocation: Phoenix's offense collapsed from 88 points through three quarters to only 13 in Q4 after the starters were shut down, while Toronto improved to 20. Aggregate remaining scoring stayed compressed even though the trailing team regressed upward.
postmortem.lesson: Large-lead Q4 unders should not be modeled as symmetric shooting regression. Explicitly price rotation shutdown for the leading team and comeback/garbage-time efficiency for the trailing team. The aggregate total can remain Under even when the trailing offense improves. Also preserve execution discipline: the wager became materially better at 176.5/-105 than the first observed 175.5/-110, but the 2.5-point model gap was still much thinner than a normal high-confidence LIVE-FLOW strike and should remain tagged as execution-dependent rather than retroactively upgraded because it won.

notes: SharpEdge end-of-third-quarter frozen projection: TOR 69, PHX 105, final 174. First observed William Hill market was 175.5 (Under -110); executed ticket was Under 176.5 at -105 for $9.33, paid $18.22. Official final: PHX 101, TOR 69. Ticket settled WON.
